title: Payer Allowance Policy: Blood Glucose Testing Strips and Supplies
content:
**A. Strip allowance.** The strips a refill on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program may ship are limited by the tier's allowance for the program's treatment class over the rolling 90 days ending on the ship date: the tier's insulin-treated allowance for an insulin-treated customer and its not-insulin-treated allowance otherwise, both counted over the strips shipped in the window including the refill being shipped, and further limited by the quantity on the written order. The strips counted are the units times the strips per billing unit of the program's test-strip refill shipments whose ship date falls in the 90 calendar days ending on and including the ship date of the refill being considered, plus that refill; replacement shipments are excluded.

*Retirement note.* The words "over the rolling 90 days ending on the ship date: the insulin-treated allowance for an insulin-treated customer and the not-insulin-treated allowance otherwise, both counted by the strips shipped in the rolling 90 days including the refill being shipped" are no longer in force as the measure of coverage when a liability notice for test strips is sized under the current above-coverage notice basis. For every refill they remain the allowance the refill itself must fit, over the rolling 90 days ending on its ship date.

**B. CGM holders.** While the customer holds an active CGM program, the allowance is the lower of the treatment-class allowance and the tier's with-CGM allowance, under the CGM holder strip allowance rule.

**C. Above the allowance.** A quantity above the allowance is covered only when a medical record with the purpose over-limit justification, documenting the testing frequency the practitioner ordered and the customer's testing log, is dated no more than the tier's above-allowance record recency, in calendar months before the ship date. The allowance then becomes the testing frequency documented in that record times 90 days. Without such a record an above-allowance quantity ships only under the advance liability notice rules, at the Larkfield cash price.

**D. Units.** Units are whole billing units: strips ship 50 to a unit (A4253) and lancets 100 to a unit (A4259), and the lancets covered are 1 for every strip covered; quantities are rounded down to whole units within the allowance.

**E. Other items.** Control solution (A4256) is covered at the tier's figure of 1 unit per rolling 90 days, a lancing device (A4258) no sooner than the tier's lancing device interval in calendar months after the previous one, and a meter (E0607) no sooner than the tier's meter replacement interval in calendar months after the meter ship date on the program, counted in calendar months from that ship date with the same calendar day allowed (the last day of the month when that day does not exist). On the self-pay tier every item is sold at the cash price without a quantity cap beyond the written order.

**F. Replacements.** A replacement never exceeds the units of the shipment it replaces and never counts toward the allowance.

**Worked example (hypothetical figures).** Allowance 300 strips; the refills shipped in the 90 days ending on the ship date hold 4 units, that is 200 strips. The refill being shipped may bring the total to 300 strips, so it may carry 100 strips, that is 2 whole units. Had 230 strips already shipped, the 70 strips left would round down to 1 unit.

**Meter interval, both sides (hypothetical).** Previous meter shipped 10 June with a 36-month interval: a meter shipping on 10 June three years later is within coverage; one shipping on 9 June that year is not.

superseded_clauses: over the rolling 90 days ending on the ship date: strips_per_90_days_insulin for an insulin-treated customer and strips_per_90_days_non_insulin otherwise, both counted by bgm_msr_strips_shipped_90d including the refill being shipped
